questions.question_text:
An investor deposits $\$850$ at the beginning of each year for $2\text{ years}$ into an account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the balance at the end of the $2\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Used $850+850(1.06)$, so the final payment earned no interest and the first earned only one year.
Added the two payments and ignored interest.
Calculated $850(1.06)^2$ for the first deposit and omitted the second deposit.

questions.solution_text:
The two payments earn two years and one year of interest respectively.
$FV=850(1.06)+850(1.06)^2$.
This is a geometric series with first term $850(1.06)$, common ratio $1.06$ and two terms.
$FV=\dfrac{850(1.06)(1.06^2-1)}{0.06}=\$1856.06$.
The other options respectively omit one period of interest from each payment, ignore all interest, or omit the second payment.

questions.question_text:
A parent deposits $\$1500$ at the beginning of each year for $10\text{ years}$ into a savings fund earning $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the future value at the end of the $10\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Treated the annuity as ordinary with end-of-year payments, omitting the extra factor of $1.07$.
Calculated the sum of payments without applying any compound interest.
Included eleven start-of-year payments and valued them at the end of year 11 instead of using ten payments over ten years.

questions.solution_text:
There are ten annual payments, earning between one and ten years of interest.
$FV=1500(1.07)+1500(1.07)^2+\dots+1500(1.07)^{10}$.
The geometric series has first term $1500(1.07)$, common ratio $1.07$ and ten terms.
$FV=\dfrac{1500(1.07)(1.07^{10}-1)}{0.07}\approx\$22175.40$.
Omitting the extra factor gives $\$20724.67$; ignoring interest gives $\$15000.00$. The remaining option uses eleven terms, so it exceeds the ten-payment balance.

questions.question_text:
Maya invests $\$200$ at the beginning of each month for $5\text{ years}$ into an account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Find the balance at the end of the $5\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Calculated future value for an ordinary annuity with end-of-month payments.
Multiplied payment by 60 months without calculating compound interest.
Used $r=0.06$ for each of the 60 monthly periods instead of dividing the annual rate by 12.

questions.solution_text:
$r=\dfrac{0.06}{12}=0.005$, $n=60$.
The 60 deposits earn between one and 60 months of interest.
$FV=200(1.005)+200(1.005)^2+\dots+200(1.005)^{60}$.
The geometric series has first term $200(1.005)$, common ratio $1.005$ and 60 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{200(1.005)(1.005^{60}-1)}{0.005}\approx\$14023.78$.
The ordinary-annuity result is $\$13954.01$, while the payments alone total $\$12000.00$. Using a monthly rate of $6\%$ produces the much larger remaining option.

questions.question_text:
A sports club deposits $\$900$ at the beginning of each quarter for $4\text{ years}$ into a reserve account earning $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly.
Find the future value at the end of the $4\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Omitted the extra quarterly factor of $1.02$, treating it as an ordinary annuity.
Calculated simple principal total ($16 \times 900$) without interest.
Used $n = 4$ years instead of $n = 16$ quarterly compounding periods.

questions.solution_text:
$r=\dfrac{0.08}{4}=0.02$, $n=16$.
The 16 payments earn between one and 16 quarters of interest.
$FV=900(1.02)+900(1.02)^2+\dots+900(1.02)^{16}$.
The geometric series has first term $900(1.02)$, common ratio $1.02$ and 16 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{900(1.02)(1.02^{16}-1)}{0.02}\approx\$17110.86$.
Removing the extra factor gives $\$16775.36$; ignoring interest gives $\$14400.00$. Four quarterly payments instead give $900(1.02+1.02^2+1.02^3+1.02^4)=\$3783.636144$, which rounds to $\$3783.64$.

questions.question_text:
A person wants to save $\$25\,000$ in $4\text{ years}$ with equal start-of-year deposits earning $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the required annual deposit $a$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Calculated payment using ordinary annuity formula (end-of-year deposits).
Divided $\$25\,000$ by 4 years without accounting for interest.
Used five payments valued at the end of year 5 instead of four payments valued at the end of year 4.

questions.solution_text:
The four annual payments earn between one and four years of interest.
$25000=a(1.065)+a(1.065)^2+a(1.065)^3+a(1.065)^4$.
The geometric series has first term $a(1.065)$, common ratio $1.065$ and four terms.
$25000=a\dfrac{1.065(1.065^4-1)}{0.065}=4.693640725625a$.
$a=\dfrac{25000}{4.693640725625}\approx\$5326.36$.
Omitting the extra factor gives $\$5672.57$; ignoring interest gives $\$6250.00$. Using five terms gives the smaller remaining deposit.

questions.question_text:
An investor deposits $\$1100$ at the beginning of each year for $3\text{ years}$ into an account earning $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the balance at the end of the $3\text{ years}$, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Used $1100+1100(1.08)+1100(1.08)^2$, omitting one year of interest from each deposit.
Added the three payments without including interest.
Calculated $1100(1.08)$ for the final deposit only and omitted the first two deposits.

questions.solution_text:
The three payments earn three, two and one years of interest respectively.
$FV=1100(1.08)+1100(1.08)^2+1100(1.08)^3$.
The geometric series has first term $1100(1.08)$, common ratio $1.08$ and three terms.
$FV=\dfrac{1100(1.08)(1.08^3-1)}{0.08}=\$3856.7232\approx\$3856.72$.
The other options use the ordinary-annuity sum, omit all interest, or include only the final payment.

questions.question_text:
A saver deposits $\$450$ at the start of each month into an account earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly for $8\text{ years}$.
Which amount gives the balance at the end of the $8\text{ years}$, rounded to the nearest cent?

options.why: Used end-of-month payments, omitting one month of interest from each of the 96 payments.
Calculated $450(96)$ and ignored interest.
Used eight monthly periods instead of the 96 monthly periods in eight years.

questions.solution_text:
$r=0.072/12=0.006$, $n=8\times12=96$.
At the end of month 96, the first payment has earned 96 months of interest and the final payment has earned one month.
$FV=450(1.006)+450(1.006)^2+\dots+450(1.006)^{96}$.
The geometric series has first term $450(1.006)$, common ratio $1.006$ and 96 terms.
$FV=\dfrac{450(1.006)(1.006^{96}-1)}{0.006}\approx\$58\,537.84$.
The other options respectively omit the extra monthly factor, ignore interest, or use only eight payments. All are smaller than the correct 96-payment balance.

questions.question_text:
A company makes annual contributions of $\$15\,000$ to an endowment fund at the beginning of each year for $20\text{ years}$. The fund earns $10\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate, to the nearest dollar, the amount to which the first contribution has grown at the end of the 20th year.

options.why: Used $15000(1.1)^{19}$, omitting the first contribution's twentieth year of interest.
Used $15000(1.1)$, calculating the grown value of the final contribution instead of the first.
Calculated $15000(20)$, the total contributed, instead of the grown value of the first contribution.

questions.solution_text:
The first contribution is paid at the start of year 1 and valued at the end of year 20, so it earns 20 full years of interest.
Its value is $15000(1.1)^{20}\approx\$100912.50$, which rounds to $\$100912$ using the unrounded value.
For comparison, $15000(1.1)^{19}$ rounds to $\$91739$, the final contribution grows to $\$16500$, and the 20 contributions total $\$300000$. This question values one specified contribution, so no annuity sum is needed.
